title: Adaptive refinement of the Boolean inductive iris in WR-90 at 10 GHz: passes from 4 mm until ΔS < 3e-3
source: The iris of the boolean-iris case (12 mm wide, 2 mm thick, centred): mode matching of TE_m0 modes at its two junctions, cascaded as generalised scattering matrices (A. Wexler, IEEE Trans. MTT 15(9):508–517, 1967), converged with 640 modes

quantities.reason: the iris' four edges make E ∝ r^{-1/3}, so uniform meshes converge as h^{4/3}: +0.0108 at 3 mm (23 166 unknowns), +0.0058 at 2 mm (61 634), +0.0044 at 1.5 mm (126 826), +0.0032 at 1.2 mm (239 344). The passes mark a few tetrahedra at the edges each time: +0.0128, +0.0047, +0.0026, +0.0014 at pass 4 (143 516 unknowns, 5.5 GB, where ΔS < 3e-3 stops it): the uniform 1.2 mm's error halved with 60 % of its unknowns
as |S11|: +1.27° at uniform 3 mm, falling with it
as |S11|; power is conserved to rounding
